notes.title: Tutorial Update - Demo v1.0.9
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I recently had a playtest session at a local event, where I had the chance to see with my own eyes how completely new players interact with the game. The poor communication has been one of the biggest issues of the game, but all my previous playtesters were already familiar with the game, so testing the onboarding has been a challenge.

I realized that most players had absolutely no clue what the game wanted them to do, so I had to guide them through the very first level before they could enjoy the game. At the end of the day, I learned that it was a necessity to explain step-by-step what the player needs to do to overcome the very first puzzle, but they also need from the very start all the knowledge needed to finish the first level.

User experience was the second issue. Some interactions were unclear, with most players overlooking important details.

In this update, I tried to fix those issues. Here is the list of changes:
- A second guide has been introduced. You can open it by pressing J (remappable), anc will show you information about how you can play the game. It will update automatically whenever a new tutorial is completed.
-  A puzzle tutorial has been introduced. It explains how panels work, and how to activate them to open doors
- A drawing tutorial has been introduced. It explains how to cast spells
- Some assets were changed to improve user experience
- Added a one-time use spell slot. This is not necessary in the demo, but I added it to show that it's available in the full game.
- Updated physics for the Wind Grasp spell.

That's all, have fun playing the demo!

notes.title: Demo Update 1.0.7 - QoL features
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

In this update I mainly added quality of life features, trying to address the confusing onboarding for some of the players who tried the demo.

[list]
[*] Introduced a manual where there is an explanation on what each unlocked spell does, and how to use it.
[*] When drawing a new spell, the spell guide will open automatically. It also always opens at the page of your currently "equipped" spell.
[*] When a new spell is unlocked, it will sparkle in the draw menu, until it's drawing is confirmed. This way, it should be easier to locate the newly unlocked spell in the list.
[*] Because of the introduction of the guide, I removed some of the pop-ups that appeared throughout the demo.
[/list]

I also optimized some of the game assets, as I received some complaints about it. The main culprits were some of the trees which had an excessively high amount of vertices. Hopefully this should improve the experience for those who encountered this issue.

Lastly, I fixed the glitches that sometime happened when flying with a platform. Dealing with physics always gives headaches, but with the current setup I didn't encounter the issue anymore, let me know if it's still not completely fixed.

That's all. I hope you enjoy the demo!

notes.title: Demo update V1.0.6
notes.content:
Dear players,

Thank you for trying out the Runa Illustra Demo and for your valuable feedback! I've been listening closely and have made several improvements to enhance game clarity, accessibility, and overall experience.

Here are some of the changes in v1.0.6:
[list]
[*] Dynamic Reticle: The reticle now changes when an interactable object is within range, helping you aim more effectively.
[*] Spell Name Display: Added an option to display spell names on the hotbar for better spell management. You can enable/disable this through the accessibility section of settings
[*] Revised drawing recognition system. It should now identify more easily shapes with asymmetrical point density.
[*] Candles can now be lit!
[/list]
I hope these and all the other changes will improve your experience! If you encounter any bugs, you can report them on [url=https://discord.gg/fHXBMG7C2U]Discord[/url]

Have fun spellcasting!
